clue.text: Dealt with cynical changes by mistake

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone handled a run of cynical alterations, and it was all an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the twelve letters of DEALT and CYNICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by mistake means doing it unintentionally, without meaning to.

clue.text: Plug more suitable for electrical accessory

parts.note: a plug is a promotional mention, an advertisement or AD
apt means suitable, so more suitable is APTER

explanation.surface: A plug that suits better makes a handy electrical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like the electrical part, but it is an advert, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter is a fitting that lets a plug or device connect to a different socket, an electrical accessory.

clue.text: Cold comfort possibly found in end

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ease means comfort, as in a life of ease

explanation.surface: Little consolation may be had when things are over.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to stop or finish, so it is a verb meaning to come to an end.

clue.text: Put off man producing washing powder?

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off
a gent is a man, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: Is the man who discourages people the one selling laundry soap?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: washing powder is one kind of cleaning agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing powder is a cleaning agent used in laundry, an example of the broader category.

clue.text: In poverty, born and died

parts.note: née, born, is used before a woman's maiden name
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone was born into hardship and died in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Need here is the noun meaning want or destitution, the state of lacking money.

clue.text: Horrible toadies purchasing Queen 'rock'

indicators.note: purchasing means taking hold of, so the scrambled letters close around the Queen
horrible suggests the word toadies is mangled into a new order

parts.note: R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Nasty sycophants buy a Queen record, the rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible' rearranges TOADIES into ASTEOID, and 'purchasing' puts R inside it. The quotes on 'rock' hint it is not music but a space rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, a rock in space.

clue.text: Inclined to use spare time

parts.note: spare means thin or meagre, lean

explanation.surface: Someone tends to make good use of their free hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare time' reads as leisure, but spare is LEAN and time is T.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, so it means tilted or tended in a direction.

clue.text: Bizarre exercise with perjurer protecting copper

indicators.note: protecting means shielding something within, so the copper sits inside

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a perjurer tells lies under oath, a liar
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A strange story of a workout alongside a lying witness shielding a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal's symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar means strange or odd, a close synonym of weird.

clue.text: Cheers fast time showing skill

parts.note: ta and cheers are both informal British thanks
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A toast during a quick spell reveals someone's ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' and 'ta' are both casual British ways of saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent is a natural ability or gift, another word for aptitude.

clue.text: Isolated workers finally quit accommodation

parts.note: isolated means set apart
men are workers, as in a boss and his men

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word quit

explanation.surface: Cut off, the staff eventually left their lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms to live in, so a form of lodging.

clue.text: Stadium is new in neighbourhood

indicators.note: in places the new letter within the word for a district

parts.note: a neighbourhood is a local area

explanation.surface: A sports ground has just opened in the district.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for sport or shows, much like a sports ground.

clue.text: Speculation of people in authority hoarding gold

indicators.note: hoarding means storing away inside, so gold goes within the people

parts.note: they is the vague word for those in charge, as in 'they say'
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Rumours that the powers that be are stockpiling bullion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' is used loosely for unnamed authorities ('they won't allow it'). OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or hypothesis, an idea not yet proven.

clue.text: Come through for Tory's first offensive

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Tory's

parts.note: rude means offensive or impolite

explanation.surface: A supporter of the Conservative leader's opening shot is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come through' is not 'succeed' but to stick out through a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out or project, poking through a surface.

clue.text: Cultivated vacant rogue facing a socialist

indicators.note: vacant means emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters of rogue

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A brainless scoundrel confronts a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Reared means raised or bred, as plants or livestock are grown and tended.

clue.text: Hatred is over and practically obliterated

indicators.note: obliterated means smashed up, so the letters are shaken into a new order
practically means almost all of the word and, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Loathing is finished and almost wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' cuts AND to AN; 'obliterated' rearranges ISOVER plus AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or disgust, close to loathing.

clue.text: Literal dash following motorway

indicators.note: following means the run comes after the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
a dash is a short fast run, a sprint

explanation.surface: A literal-minded person races along after the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' is printers' jargon for a typo, not an adjective. The M1 is the main London-to-Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a literal is a typographical slip in a letter, a typo.

clue.text: Lord accepts resistance over capable extortionist

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the lord holds the other pieces

parts.note: a peer is a lord
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
fit means able or capable, as in fit for duty

explanation.surface: A nobleman takes on opposition from a competent blackmailer.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiteer makes excessive gains by exploiting shortages, like an extortioner.

clue.text: One appreciates some reggae's the technique

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A music lover admires part of the craft of reggae.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone with a keen sense of beauty and art, one who appreciates it.

clue.text: Break bed's head, preferably clutching sweetheart

indicators.note: head of the word bed's means its first letter
clutching means holding tightly inside

parts.note: rather means preferably, as in I'd rather
the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet

explanation.surface: Smash the bedhead, ideally while hugging your darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' reads as a darling but means the heart of sweet, its middle letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short rest or pause, a break from activity.

clue.text: Most undressed are almost wearing top

indicators.note: wearing means one piece is clothed by the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: best means top, as in the best or top student

indicators.note: almost means the word are lacks its last letter

explanation.surface: Being nearly naked, they are just about wearing a top.
explanation.definitionFit: Barest is the superlative of bare, naked, so it means least clothed.

clue.text: Regrets doctors taking pot

indicators.note: taking means taking in, holding the pot inside

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor, so doctors are MOS
an urn is a pot or vase

explanation.surface: Medics who use cannabis regret it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' looks like cannabis, but it is a vessel, URN.
explanation.definitionFit: To mourn is to grieve or lament, so mourns means feels sorrow over, regrets.

clue.text: Devout transgress about to embrace church

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug within, so the church sits between the pieces

parts.note: to sin is to transgress
re means about or concerning
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pious person sins but is about to hug the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and heartfelt, as devout feeling is wholehearted.

clue.text: Ring of wires on a telephone

indicators.note: of means taken from within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The sound of telephone cables ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks a run of letters inside 'wires on a telephone'.
explanation.definitionFit: To resonate is to echo or reverberate, as a bell does when struck.

clue.text: Material needs yarn left over? Not initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the words before it is taken

explanation.surface: A fabric that needs yarn left over? Not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' reads as 'not at first', but 'Not' is the last word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre and the fabric woven from it, a material.

clue.text: Squabble during lunch

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
in means during, as in in the night

explanation.surface: An argument over the midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is a light meal, especially in India, eaten at midday.

clue.text: Romp dressing nearly excessively for bed

indicators.note: dressing means wrapping around, so the fun is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: a romp is boisterous play, fun

indicators.note: nearly drops the last letter

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too much

explanation.surface: A frolic, wearing almost too little, ends in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style mattress used for sleeping, a type of bed.

clue.text: Feeble politician supporting endless fabrication

indicators.note: supporting means the politician sits beneath, holding up the other piece in a down clue
endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: a fabrication is a lie
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A weak MP props up a never-ending falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means lacking firmness or energy, weak and floppy.

clue.text: Bobbin with coils around

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: coils are loops

explanation.surface: A reel with thread wound round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a reel or cylinder on which thread is wound, like a bobbin.

clue.text: Huge opening cut earthquake's start and middle?

parts.note: epic means huge in scale

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, losing the last letter

parts.note: an entry is an opening or way in

indicators.note: start means the first letter of the word earthquake's

explanation.surface: A massive gap ripped open as an earthquake begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'middle' as a loose definition: the centre of something, as of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the central point of something, the heart of it, as well as the ground point above a quake's focus.

clue.text: Nicer pet name could give one licence

indicators.note: could give suggests the letters could be rearranged to produce something else

explanation.surface: A nicer pet name might earn a permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licence' here is not a permit but excess, lack of restraint. 'one' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence can mean excessive freedom or indulgence, much like a lack of self-restraint.
